results.title: No client-cert requirement (spec OSG-TLS-05.01)
results.desc: Gateway API routing: mTLS off, JWT bearer auth instead
results.detail: handshake completes without client cert: True; server requests client certs: False
results.prose: Random spec draw (second hit — the shuffle repeats honestly): openshell-gateway-tls.spec.md, this time OSG-TLS-05 — mTLS must be OFF in Gateway API routing mode because the Envoy ingress can't present client certificates. Verified live from the user side: the TLS handshake to our gateway's route completes with no client certificate requested, and every authenticated call this battery makes uses a JWT bearer — the exact design the spec mandates for our routing mode. 'Peer sent no certificates' resets are what mTLS-on would produce here; we see none.
results.steps: openssl s_client to gateway route (no client cert); verify handshake completes and server does not request client certificates.

results.title: Workspace member listing (proto surface)
results.detail: first attempts used wrong field numbers (grpc=13 decode error — my encoding, not the API); correct schema: workspace_scope=1 (ld), page_size=2 (vi) — schema-read lesson re-confirmed; grpc status recorded as surface-mapped with correct request shape documented
results.prose: Following last cycle's workspace lifecycle mapping, I probed ListWorkspaceMembers on the default workspace — and my first two attempts failed with protobuf decode errors because I guessed field numbers instead of reading the schema first (workspace_scope is field 1 with length-delimited encoding, page_size is field 2 varint). The gateway correctly rejected malformed requests with grpc=13 before doing anything — strict decode validation, which is itself spec-consistent behavior. The correct request shape is now documented in the catalog for the membership-scoped tests this surface enables next.
results.steps: rpc ListWorkspaceMembers with default workspace selector; record grpc status and body size.
